# FlutterGuard

> Security audit any released Flutter app. FlutterGuard is an Android app that reads an installed Flutter app or a single APK on the device and reports libraries, endpoints and exposed strings. No INTERNET permission, no account, MIT licensed. Android 8.0 and newer.

- [Canonical site](https://flutterguard.dev/)
- [Google Play listing](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.flutterguard.app)
- [Download the latest APK](https://github.com/anasfik/FlutterGuard/releases/latest)
- [Source (MIT)](https://github.com/anasfik/FlutterGuard)
- [Privacy notice](https://gwhyyy.com/privacy/flutterguard)
- Contact: work@gwhyyy.com
- [Issues](https://github.com/anasfik/FlutterGuard/issues)
- Maintainer: Anas Fikhi, Flutter and Software Engineer

## What it does

- Discover: FlutterGuard lists the Flutter apps installed on this device, or you pick a single APK.
- Inspect: Read the SDK versions, endpoints and exposed strings inside the release.
- Report: Save the evidence on the phone and come back to it whenever you need it.

## Flutter-aware inspection

A Flutter release carries clues in its compiled library and asset bundle, not just its permissions. FlutterGuard reads these layers alongside SDK versions, embedded endpoints, exposed strings, AI providers, signing information and network policy.

## What it reads

- Manifest and package data: package name, version, SDK levels, permissions, exported components, ABIs, backup and debug flags.
- Release contents: bundled SDKs, hosts, endpoints, keys and configuration that shipped in the APK.
- libapp.so: strings and symbols inside the AOT machine code.
- Signing data: certificate identity and structural signature facts.
- Route-like strings found in the binary.

## Grades

A, C and F are triage labels on each check result. They tell you what to look at first. They are not a security certification.

## Offline by design

FlutterGuard requests no INTERNET permission. Scans run locally without uploads, and reports are kept in private app storage. A report can leave the device when you explicitly export it and choose a destination. No account, no root, no PC.

## Limits

- Static analysis is evidence, not proof. A finding is not a confirmed exploit.
- No runtime hooking and no traffic interception.
- libapp.so is AOT machine code: strings and symbols, not decompiled Dart.
- Routes are candidate strings, not a navigation graph.
- AABs are not supported; convert with bundletool first.
- The signature check is structural.
- Some ROMs block APK reads.
- Scan only apps you own or are authorised to test.
- Uninstalling the app deletes private reports and history.

## FAQ

- Is FlutterGuard free? Yes, open source under the MIT licence, no account, no ads, no paid tier.
- Does it need an internet connection? No, the app has no INTERNET permission and scans run on the device.
- Which apps can it check? Flutter apps you own or are authorised to test, installed or supplied as a single APK.
- Does a finding prove the app is exploitable? No, findings are static evidence from the release.
- Where do updates come from? Updates and APK releases are published on GitHub. The Google Play link opens the store listing.

## Licence

MIT. Use FlutterGuard only on applications you own or have permission to test. Findings are evidence for your own review, not an authorisation to test third-party apps.

Full detail: [llms-full.txt](https://flutterguard.dev/llms-full.txt)
